title: Choose the visual world for Auto One Egypt
question: The roll assigned the Departure Board. Keep it, take the winning challenger, or re-roll.

options.label: Departure Board Network
options.lineage: Cairo microbus route plates, bilingual metro enamel signage, split-flap departure boards
options.thesis: The minisite is a live board of a dealer network: every car is a destination, every relationship a line you can take.
options.viewport: A full-width board strip names the showroom and today's arrivals, and the featured car takes the largest bay as the next departure with its call action set beside it.
options.risk: Rows can read like a timetable and bury the offer unless the featured car owns the largest bay.

raised.raise: Every shelf keeps a numbered destination you can key, and the whole board is fully keyboard-operable.
Every edge of the business graph is labeled on the board rather than hidden behind a tab.
State rides row density and flap motion instead of adding a second accent color.
A structural hazard diagonal marks the one row that is genuinely live.

options.label: Glazing Partition
options.lineage: steel-framed glass partition walls from a glazier's workshop
options.thesis: The page is the showroom's own glass-and-black-metal wall: one pane per statement, and the wide panes hold the cars.
options.viewport: Full-height bays read left to right down a corridor; the centre bay is a 21:9 pane for the featured car, lit amber when selected, and the call action sits in its own small pane.
options.case: Wins on both axes: it is the material an Egyptian buyer already stands inside, and a pane is an honest frame for real photography instead of a fake one.
options.risk: Corporate glazing, if the saturated notes never fire and every pane stays clear.

options.label: Teletext Page 302
options.lineage: broadcast teletext magazines on a 40 by 24 character grid
options.thesis: The catalog as a broadcast index: three-digit pages instead of sections, and a subpage carousel you can hold still.
options.viewport: P302 header counts pages in the corner, double-height title over numbered rows, and the featured shot rotates as a subpage with a HOLD flag.
options.case: Holds clarity: its timed subpage rotation and HOLD control already are a cinematic carousel with a pause key.
options.risk: Retro novelty, if the 40-cell lattice is not kept exact.

options.label: Busytown Cross-Section
options.case: Loses identification: a picture-book cutaway is not how a Cairo buyer reads a car purchase, and it undercuts a premium offer.
options.kept: Its total-labeling discipline is now a named raise on the board.

options.label: Moire Gallery
options.case: Loses identification and clarity: the white cube is not the buyer's world, and line-frequency contrast would fight product photography.
options.kept: Its state-without-color grammar is now a named raise on the board.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.case: Loses identification: a 2 a.m. modem board is the audience's tool nostalgia, not their car-buying scene.
options.kept: Its numbered-exit keyboard routing is now a named raise on the board.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.case: Loses identification: quoted caps naming the obvious is fashion stockroom irony, and it reads as a joke on a six-figure purchase.
options.kept: Its structural hazard diagonal is now a named raise on the board.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A 21:9 dark hero carousel with glass overlays, a filmstrip, and a spec strip, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Cinematic photo band edge to edge, caption in a glass plate, thumbnails beneath, WhatsApp action pinned bottom-right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other luxury car site, which is exactly what a buyer expects to see.
